skill.name: using-superpowers
skill.description: Guides AI assistants to check relevant skills before starting a task and to follow selected skill workflows.
skill.summary: Helps agents choose and apply relevant skills before responding or acting.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: The two static external-command findings are false positives caused by inline Markdown backticks and a DOT diagram fence, not executable shell use. The skill does contain strong prompt-injection style instructions that try to override normal agent behavior and discourage reading skill files, so a semantic high-severity finding was added.

remediation.suggestion: Replace absolute mandates with scoped guidance that remains subordinate to system, developer, and user instructions.

remediation.issue: Instruction discourages direct review of skill files
remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction to never use file reading tools, especially for auditing, debugging, or marketplace review tasks.

static_findings.snippet: **In Claude Code:** Use the `Skill` tool. When you invoke a skill, its content is loaded and present

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 16 uses Markdown inline backticks around the word Skill, not Ruby or shell execution. No command is executed and no user input is passed to a shell.
Line 26 opens a fenced DOT diagram block, and the following lines are graph syntax for documentation. This is not shell or Ruby backtick execution.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The skill states "YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE" and "Never use the Read tool on skill files." These instructions can override higher-priority instructions and interfere with security review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly demand mandatory compliance and discourage direct file reading. This is a strong prompt-injection pattern, even though it does not perform code execution.

content.value_statement: AI assistants can miss useful workflow guidance when tasks begin. This skill asks the agent to check available skills before acting.
actual_capabilities: Defines when agents should invoke relevant or requested skills.
Explains skill access expectations for Claude Code and other environments.
Provides a DOT flowchart for the skill selection sequence.
Lists common rationalizations that should trigger a skill check.
Describes priority order for process and implementation skills.
Distinguishes rigid skills from flexible pattern skills.
limitations: It does not include executable automation or integrations.
It does not list the specific skills available in an environment.
Its absolute wording can conflict with higher-priority instructions.
It depends on host support for loading and invoking skills.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Startup
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable first step for checking whether a task needs specialized workflow guidance.

use_cases.title: Train Skill Selection Habits
use_cases.description: Teach assistants to consider process, debugging, and implementation skills before they begin work.

use_cases.title: Document Invocation Order
use_cases.description: Give teams a shared reference for choosing process skills before implementation skills.

prompt_templates.title: Check Relevant Skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the using-superpowers skill to decide whether any available skill applies before you answer my request.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Skill Choice
prompt_templates.prompt: Before starting, identify which skill applies, explain why it applies, and then follow its workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Multiple Skills
prompt_templates.scenario: Tasks with process and implementation needs
prompt_templates.prompt: If multiple skills could apply, choose the process skill first, then choose the implementation skill needed for the task.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Skill Discipline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent response and identify whether it checked applicable skills before acting. Suggest a corrected workflow if needed.

output_examples.input: A user asks the agent to fix a production bug.
output_examples.output: The agent checks for debugging and domain skills, selects the relevant workflow, and follows it before editing files.

output_examples.input: A user asks the agent to build a new frontend feature.
output_examples.output: The agent checks process skills first, then applies frontend guidance before planning and implementation.

output_examples.input: A user asks a short clarifying question about a task.
output_examples.output: The agent considers whether a skill applies before asking or answering the clarification.

best_practices: Keep skill guidance subordinate to system, developer, and user instructions.
Use the skill only where the host environment supports skill discovery.
State the selected skill and purpose before substantial work begins.
anti_patterns: Do not use absolute skill instructions to override platform security rules.
Do not skip required clarification when no relevant skill exists.
Do not block file review or audit commands required by the task.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It tells an agent to check for relevant skills before responding or taking action.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is written guidance and contains no executable scripts.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Can it choose a skill automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide the agent's decision, but actual skill loading depends on the host environment.

faq.question: What should users be careful about?
faq.answer: Its mandatory wording should not override higher-priority instructions or security review requirements.

faq.question: Is it best for coding tasks only?
faq.answer: No. It is a general process skill for any task where specialized guidance may apply.
